{{Short description|Research concept}}
'''Imperfect induction''' is the process of inferring from a [[Sample (statistics)|sample]] of a group to what is characteristic of the whole group.<ref>Ary, D., Jacobs, L., Razavieh A., and Sorensen, C. (2006). ''Introduction to Research in Education'' (7th ed.). New York: Wadsworth Group.</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/researchineducat0000turn|title=Research in education: An Introduction|last=Turney|first=Billy Lawrence|last2=Robb|first2=George Paul|publisher=Dryden Press|year=1971|isbn=0030890047|location=Hinsdale, Ill.|chapter=Introduction: The Scientific Approach to Research|oclc=267876|chapter-url=https://ww2.odu.edu/~jritz/attachments/635_reined.htm|url-access=registration}}</ref>
